what_it_does: Diffusion Transformers — a class of AI image-generation model that works by gradually denoising a picture through many sequential steps — are slow and energy-hungry at inference time because they repeat nearly identical computations at each step. RADiT identifies blocks of computation whose inputs barely change between one denoising step and the next, and simply reuses the output from the previous step for those blocks instead of recomputing them. Two custom hardware modules manage this: one dynamically decides how similar two consecutive inputs need to be before reuse is safe, and another compresses and compares the relevant features efficiently in hardware. The result is faster, lower-energy image generation with minimal loss in output quality.
